item.title: SF TD signed off on two non-charity entities, court told
item.description: The High Court has been told that the Sinn Féin TD Aengus Ó Snodaigh in his capacity as chairperson of the charity Liberty Recycling signed off on the establishment of two other related entities which were not charities.

item.title: Former principal, 91, jailed over 'brazen' abuse of pupil
item.description: A former principal of De La Salle National School in Waterford city has been sentenced to four years and three months in prison for abusing a child, with the final year suspended.

item.title: O'Neill says DUP ending engagements 'supremacist'
item.description: The Democratic Unionist Party is to end joint engagements of Stormont's First Ministers' office in a row with Sinn Féin over Drumcree, a move Michelle O'Neill called "arrogant and supremacist".

item.title: Death toll from Spanish train crash rises to 74
item.description: The death toll from the crash involving two high-speed trains in Spain has risen to 74 from 69, according to the transport ministry.

item.title: Reported drug-related intimidation just 'tip of iceberg'
item.description: Criminals are selling drug debts on to other groups who enforce what is allegedly owed at a higher amount, the Garda Commissioner has said.

item.title: Eisenkot warns of campaign to 'delegitimise' election
item.description: Israel's chief opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot has warned that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was working to delegitimise election results with his allegations of malfeasance by Arab parties.

item.title: Enoch Burke banned from going within 100 metres of school
item.description: Enoch Burke has been banned from going within 100 metres of a school in Co Westmeath after a judge amended an order against him.

item.title: U2 to wrap next tour in Ireland - but no dates yet
item.description: U2 have reassured fans at home that they will be announcing Irish shows as they unveiled UK and European dates for their upcoming tour, Carnaval de Luz Presents: The Greatest Show on Earth.

item.title: Children who were mistreated at crèche awarded €36,000
item.description: A brother and sister who alleged they were mistreated at a crèche, which became the subject of RTÉ's "Behind Closed Doors" exposé, have been awarded €36,000 damages.

item.title: Late Late Show reveals Halloween Special line-up
item.description: Fionnula Flanagan will be among Patrick Kielty's guests on Friday's Late Late Show Halloween Special on RTÉ One and RTÉ Player.

item.title: Foley's case to stop CAB seizing home adjourned
item.description: Convicted criminal Martin Foley, also known as The Viper, has had his challenge against the sale of his home by the Criminal Assets Bureau adjourned to next week.

item.title: 9,000-year-old 'Swiss Army kit' found in Co Wicklow
item.description: Researchers at the Threecastles Solar Farm near Blessington have discovered what is believed to be the oldest archaeological site ever excavated in Co Wicklow.

item.title: Suspected data breach of employment permit online system
item.description: A suspected data breach is being investigated involving the Employment Permit Online System operated by the Department of Enterprise.

item.title: 14 killed in Russian strike on train station in Ukraine
item.description: A Russian drone slammed into a busy platform at a railway station in Ukraine's Dnipro today, killing at least 14 people in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called a "horrific" attack that demands a response from Kyiv's allies.

item.title: EU, Canada want to bring relationship to 'highest level'
item.description: The EU and Canada want to bring their relationship to the "highest level possible" as they face a "world of growing rivalries," Ursula von der Leyen said ahead of a meeting with Canadian leader Mark Carney.

item.title: €8bn in bailout loans to be repaid early under Govt plans
item.description: The Government is planning to repay €8 billion in loans received during the financial crisis ahead of schedule.

item.title: Trump calls Brazil election a 'disgraceful situation'
item.description: US President Donald Trump has described Brazil's presidential election as "disgraceful".

item.title: Ten years on, new details emerge of threats to killed campaigner
item.description: 63-year-old Michael McCoy was found dead in woodland near his home in the Dublin mountains having suffered blunt force trauma to his head and face

item.title: Murder trial told wife prayed over unconscious husband
item.description: A woman has given evidence at a murder trial of praying over her 80-year-old husband when she found him unconscious and bloodied on the ground outside their home in Tipperary.

item.title: Prison service proposed sentence cuts due to overcrowding
item.description: Irish jails were so overcrowded that a proposal to cut 40 days from the sentence of every prisoner in the State was put forward by authorities struggling to find more space.

item.title: ECB keeps rates unchanged but points to inflation risk
item.description: The European Central Bank left interest rates unchanged in a well-telegraphed move today but warned that inflation risks were on the rise from surging energy costs, which may solidify market bets for a December rate hike.

item.title: Gallagher and Reilly come in as Ireland make two changes
item.description: Niamh Gallagher and Aoibheann Reilly have both been handed starts for Ireland's final WXV Global Series game of the season.

item.title: Defence Force members felt 'undervalued and overworked'
item.description: The Chief of Staff of the Irish Defence Forces has said updated definitions of acceptable and unacceptable behaviour across the organisation have become part of its training, briefings and regulations.

item.title: Lagarde announces resignation after months of speculation
item.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announced her resignation today, ending months of speculation about her future just as Europe enters a period of rising economic volatility and divisive electoral politics.

item.title: Third quarter new home completions up by 10% - CSO
item.description: There was a 10.4% increase in the number of new homes built in the third quarter of this year, from July to September, as 10,154 dwellings were finished.

item.title: Social Democrats call for public register of data centres
item.description: The Social Democrats have called for a public register of data centres to track their locations, carbon emissions, energy requirements and water usage.

item.title: Russell Brand's wife tells court he is 'caring, kind'
item.description: Russell Brand's wife has told his rape trial her husband is "caring" and "kind" and there is honesty at the centre of their marriage.

item.title: Govt taking summit security 'extraordinarily seriously'
item.description: Ireland has the capabilities to protect European leaders who will gather in Dublin for two major summits next month, the Tánaiste has said.

item.title: Turtle returns to sea after 22 years at Kerry aquarium
item.description: A sea turtle, affectionately known as the 'queen of the shark tank' at Dingle Aquarium, has been released back into the sea after living at the aquarium for the past 22 years.

item.title: Is the Republican stronghold of Texas turning blue?
item.description: Polling shows that Democrat James Talarico is neck-and-neck with Republican Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race, writes Jackie Fox.

item.title: 26% of adults have experienced sexual violence - report
item.description: Just over a quarter of the population have experienced sexual violence as an adult, according to a report.

item.title: McDonald among Mayo's All-Stars after dream summer
item.description: All-Ireland SFC champions Mayo have secured six places on this year's PwC Football All-Star team, with eight different counties represented on the selection.

item.title: Harris rejects 'characterisation' of call with O'Donovan
item.description: Tánaiste Simon Harris has rejected the "characterisation" of his phone call with Patrick O'Donovan hours before the media minister became ill at an EU event.

item.title: Anti-immigration campaigner cleared of false claim charge
item.description: A high-profile, anti-immigration campaigner has been cleared of a charge of making a false claim that an asylum seeker exposed himself on a bus to a teenage girl.

item.title: Irish eyes on Joanne McNally for Celeb Traitors reveal
item.description: BBC One's The Celebrity Traitors will reveal tonight whether comedian Joanne McNally or actress Sharon Rooney will be banished after last week's cliffhanger left their fates hanging in the balance.

item.title: US warns allies of potential Iran strikes after midterms
item.description: US officials have told several Middle East countries and regional allies to be prepared for potential renewed military action against Iran after next week's US midterm elections.

item.title: Christine Lagarde: The outsider who led the ECB her way
item.description: Christine Lagarde's decision to step down early as European Central Bank president ends an eventful seven years at an institution she was never expected to lead.

item.title: EU energy ministers to discuss soaring fuel prices
item.description: EU energy ministers will meet to discuss energy security ahead of winter as the wars in Iran, Ukraine and Yemen send oil and natural gas prices soaring.

item.title: Kompany released from hospital after training collapse
item.description: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has been discharged from hospital following his collapse last week.

item.title: Restored nature hits record level, still off target - UN
item.description: Countries are restoring about 252 million hectares of nature, a record level according to a United Nations report, but this still falls short of global 2030 targets.

item.title: Initiative needed to define Irish unity debate - Martin
item.description: A new initiative is required to challenge all traditions to engage with "hard evidence" on different constitutional frameworks around unity, the Taoiseach has said.

item.title: Social worker tells murder trial of concern for pensioner
item.description: A social worker has told a jury at the Central Criminal Court of her concern for Josephine 'Josie' Ray in the months before her murder at her home in Nenagh, Co Tipperary two years ago.

item.title: Govt says opposition want to 'slow-walk' triple lock bill
item.description: The controversial bill to remove the triple lock from Irish law will not be debated by an Oireachtas committee until at least the second half of November.

item.title: Bolsonaro says he is Brazil's leader after fleeing to US
item.description: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has insisted that he is his country's rightful leader after arriving in the United States to start a self-imposed exile.

item.title: Israeli election 'stolen' by Arab parties, says Likud
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud accused Arab parties of having stolen the country's election, after partial results showed they could play a kingmaking role in forming a new government.

item.title: Inquest jury recommends garda restraint training
item.description: A verdict of death by misadventure has been recorded into the death of a man who became unresponsive after being held in a prone position by gardaí.

item.title: Putin salutes Musk's 'genius' as Russia follows Starlink
item.description: President Vladimir Putin has hailed Elon Musk as a genius, acknowledging Russia is only beginning to roll out its answer to his Starlink satellite internet system.

item.title: Vance contacted top Iran security official - US outlet
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance has contacted Iran's security chief in a bid to revive peace talks that could head off a renewed American assault on the Islamic republic, the Wall Street Journal has reported.

item.title: NI secretary ban on Drumcree march lawful, court rules
item.description: A Belfast court has ruled that the Northern Secretary made a lawful decision when he banned the Drumcree parade earlier this month.

item.title: Jury discharged in case of man accused of father's murder
item.description: A jury has been discharged two weeks into the trial of a man accused of murdering his father at the apartment they shared in Dublin.

item.title: Tommy Robinson found guilty of harassing two journalists
item.description: Far-right activist Tommy Robinson has been convicted of harassing two journalists and causing them to fear violence.

item.title: Harris denies 'heated' O'Donovan call on day he fell ill
item.description: Tánaiste Simon Harris has confirmed he spoke to Patrick O'Donovan on the phone shortly before the Minister for Culture fell ill and was taken to hospital.

item.title: Girl, 8, attacked by wolf in German wildlife park
item.description: A young girl has been attacked by a wolf and badly injured in a German wildlife park, police said, adding that the eight-year-old was taken to hospital by rescue helicopter.

item.title: McClean and Derry City mutually agree to part ways
item.description: James McClean's second spell at Derry City has come to an end after the player and the club mutually agreed to terminate his contract with immediate effect.

item.title: Hospital overcrowding highest recorded this year - INMO
item.description: There has been a further rise in hospital overcrowding with 824 patients waiting for admission to a bed, according to the Irish Nurses and Midwives Organisation.

item.title: Stroke survivor saved after speaking 'gibberish' on call
item.description: A man is urging people to be aware of the stroke symptoms after he was saved by a colleague who noticed he was speaking "complete gibberish" on a work call.

item.title: 68% of households within 2km of high-frequency bus stop
item.description: New figures from the Central Statistics Office reveal that eight in ten households are located within two kilometres of a bus stop while almost seven in ten are near a high-frequency bus service.

item.title: UK budget pledges billions in household supports
item.description: British finance minister John Healey has announced support to help households through the "global economic storms" with subsidies for energy bills and a freeze in fuel duty for drivers in the first budget plan of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government.

item.title: Brand tells court he was 'wrong' to use his fame for sex
item.description: Russell Brand told jurors at his rape trial he has dedicated much of his life to "beyond reckless philandering and idiocy", and admitted he had been wrong to use his fame to get sex.

item.title: Man, 92, guilty of indecent assault on sisters in 1970s
item.description: A 92-year-old Co Clare man who paid out €60,000 two years ago to two orphaned sisters has been found guilty of eight counts of indecent assault.
